name: Banana bread
summary: A moist loaf of mashed ripe banana, brown sugar and melted butter. Cuts into 10 slices.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Mash the ripe bananas, then beat in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the plain flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, plus the cinnamon and chopped walnuts if using.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean; cool and cut into 10 slices.
notes: The banana line is peeled weight: about 3 large ripe bananas.

name: Chocolate chip banana bread
summary: Banana bread with dark chocolate chips folded through instead of walnuts. Cuts into 10 slices.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Mash the ripe bananas, then beat in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the plain flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, then the chocolate chips.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean; cool and cut into 10 slices.
notes: Chocolate chips are logged as 45-59% dark chocolate; swap for milk chocolate if that is what you use.

name: Blueberry muffins
summary: Soft, oil-based muffins studded with fresh blueberries. Makes 12.
method: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the plain flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl; whisk the eggs, milk, sunflower oil and vanilla in a jug.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry until only just combined, then fold in the blueberries.
Divide between the cases and bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
notes: Frozen blueberries work too; add them straight from the freezer.

name: Chocolate muffins
summary: Cocoa muffins with chunks of dark chocolate in place of the blueberries. Makes 12.
method: Heat the oven to 200 °C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the plain flour, cocoa, sugar, baking powder and salt; whisk the eggs, milk, sunflower oil and vanilla in a jug.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry until just combined and fold in the chocolate chunks.
Divide between the cases and bake for 18 to 20 minutes until risen and springy.

name: Oat cookies
summary: Chewy oat cookies with butter, brown sugar and a little cinnamon. Makes 16.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line two trays.
Cream the soft butter with the brown sugar and white sugar, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the plain flour, oats, bicarbonate of soda, salt, cinnamon and the raisins if using.
Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on the trays and bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden at the edges.

name: Chocolate chip cookies
summary: Classic butter cookies with crisp edges, soft middles and plenty of chocolate chips. Makes 16.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line two trays.
Cream the soft butter with the brown sugar and white sugar, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix in the plain flour, bicarbonate of soda and salt, then the chocolate chips.
Roll into 16 balls, space well apart on the trays and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft in the middle.
notes: Chocolate chips are logged as 45-59% dark chocolate; swap for milk chocolate if used.

name: Flapjacks
summary: Chewy oat bars baked in butter, honey and brown sugar. Cuts into 16.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the butter, honey and brown sugar together, then stir in the oats and salt.
Press into the tin and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden at the edges.
Mark into 16 squares while warm and cut when cold.
notes: British flapjacks usually use golden syrup, which has no catalogue record; this recipe uses honey instead, so the totals are for a honey flapjack.

name: Chocolate brownies
summary: Dense, fudgy brownies made with melted dark chocolate and butter. Cuts into 16.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20 cm square tin.
Melt the dark chocolate and butter together over a pan of simmering water, then cool slightly.
Whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla until thick, fold in the chocolate, then sift in the plain flour, cocoa and salt and fold until smooth.
Pour into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until just set with a slight wobble; cool and cut into 16.

name: Vanilla sponge cake with jam
summary: A two-layer butter sponge sandwiched with jam and dusted with icing sugar. Cuts into 10.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins.
Beat the soft butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla.
Fold in the self-raising flour and baking powder, then the milk, and divide between the tins.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until springy; cool, sandwich with the jam and dust with the icing sugar.

name: Chocolate cake with ganache
summary: A butter and cocoa sponge covered in a dark chocolate and cream ganache. Cuts into 12.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and grease and line a 23 cm round tin.
Beat the soft butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla.
Fold in the self-raising flour and cocoa, alternating with the milk, then spoon into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes; cool.
For the ganache, heat the double cream until steaming, pour it over the chopped dark chocolate, stir until smooth and spread over the cooled cake.

name: Baked vanilla cheesecake
summary: A creamy baked cheesecake on a buttery digestive base, with lemon and vanilla. Cuts into 12.
method: Heat the oven to 160 °C. Crush the digestive biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into the tin; bake for 10 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese, sugar and cornflour until smooth, then beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by the soured cream, vanilla, lemon zest and lemon juice.
Pour over the base and bake for 50 to 55 minutes until set at the edges with a slight wobble in the middle.
Turn off the oven and leave the cheesecake inside with the door ajar for 1 hour, then chill overnight before cutting into 12.
notes: Digestive biscuits are estimated from the catalogue digestive record, which is a US graham-cracker proxy and a little leaner than typical digestives.

name: No-bake strawberry cheesecake
summary: A set cream cheese and whipped cream filling on a digestive base, topped with fresh strawberries. Cuts into 10.
method: Crush the digestive biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into the tin; chill.
Beat the cream cheese with the icing sugar, vanilla and lemon juice until smooth, then whip the double cream to soft peaks and fold it in.
Spread over the base and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight until set.
Top with the halved strawberries and cut into 10.
notes: Digestive biscuits are estimated from the catalogue digestive record, a US graham-cracker proxy.

name: Creamy rice pudding
summary: Pudding rice simmered slowly in whole milk with sugar, butter and vanilla, finished with nutmeg.
method: Rinse the pudding rice and put it in a heavy saucepan with the milk, sugar and butter.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, stirring often, for 30 to 35 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir in the vanilla and serve warm or cold with a little grated nutmeg.

name: Semolina pudding with jam
summary: Semolina cooked in milk with sugar and vanilla until smooth and thick, served with a spoonful of jam.
method: Warm the milk in a saucepan, then whisk in the semolina and sugar in a thin stream.
Simmer, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes until thick and smooth, then stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm with a spoonful of jam on top if you like.

name: Apple and blackberry crumble
summary: Sweetened cooking apples and blackberries under a buttery oat and demerara crumble.
method: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Peel, core and slice the cooking apples and toss them in the dish with the blackberries, caster sugar and cinnamon.
Rub the cold butter into the plain flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the demerara sugar and oats.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: The apple line is peeled and cored weight.

name: Plum crumble
summary: Halved plums with a little sugar and cinnamon under a buttery oat and demerara crumble.
method: Heat the oven to 190 °C. Halve and stone the plums and toss them in the dish with the caster sugar and cinnamon.
Rub the cold butter into the plain flour until it looks like breadcrumbs, then stir in the demerara sugar and oats.
Scatter the crumble over the fruit and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
notes: The plum line is stoned weight.

name: Baked apples with sultanas
summary: Whole cored apples stuffed with sultanas, brown sugar, butter and cinnamon and baked until soft.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Core the apples and score a line around the middle of each so the skin does not burst.
Mix the sultanas, brown sugar and cinnamon, pack into the apples and top each with a piece of the butter.
Stand in a dish with the water and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until soft.
notes: The apple line is the weight of 4 whole apples before coring (about 200 g each); the app counts only the edible part.

name: Strawberry yogurt ice pops
summary: Greek yogurt blended with strawberries and honey and frozen in moulds. Makes 6.
method: Blend the strawberries with the honey, then stir or ripple through the Greek yogurt.
Spoon into six moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.

name: Mango and banana smoothie ice pops
summary: A mango, banana and orange juice smoothie frozen in moulds. Makes 6.
method: Blend the mango, banana and orange juice until smooth, adding the yogurt if you want a creamier pop.
Pour into six moulds, add sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
notes: Fruit lines are peeled, stoned weight.

name: Homemade granola bars
summary: Baked oat bars with almonds, sunflower seeds and raisins, bound with honey, butter and brown sugar. Cuts into 12.
method: Heat the oven to 170 °C and line a 20 cm square tin.
Mix the oats, chopped almonds, sunflower seeds, raisins, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Melt the honey, butter and brown sugar together, pour over the dry mixture and stir until coated.
Press firmly into the tin and bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden; cool completely before cutting into 12.

name: Peanut butter oat bites
summary: No-bake bites of oats, peanut butter, honey and chocolate chips. Makes 16.
method: Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey and vanilla until the mixture holds together.
Stir in the chocolate chips, roll into 16 balls and chill for 30 minutes to firm up.

name: Chocolate yogurt bowl
summary: Greek yogurt stirred with cocoa and honey, topped with strawberries and grated dark chocolate.
method: Stir the cocoa and honey into the Greek yogurt until smooth.
Top with the sliced strawberries and grate over the dark chocolate.

name: Carrot cake with cream cheese icing
summary: A spiced oil-based carrot cake with walnuts and sultanas, topped with cream cheese icing. Cuts into 12.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 23 cm round tin.
Mix the self-raising flour, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon and brown sugar; whisk the sunflower oil with the eggs and stir them in.
Fold in the grated carrots, chopped walnuts and sultanas, spoon into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes; cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese, soft butter and icing sugar until smooth and spread over the top before cutting into 12.

name: Lemon drizzle cake
summary: A lemon-zested butter loaf soaked with a crunchy lemon and sugar drizzle. Cuts into 10.
method: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 900 g loaf tin.
Beat the soft butter and caster sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs and lemon zest.
Fold in the self-raising flour and milk, spoon into the tin and bake for 40 to 45 minutes.
Mix the lemon juice with the drizzle sugar, prick the hot cake all over and spoon the drizzle over; cool in the tin before cutting into 10.
